headline: Quantum teleportation method uses weaker entanglement to transfer encoded information
summary: Over the past several decades, researchers have demonstrated quantum teleportation, the transfer of one quantum system's state to another, in a range of systems. headline: Wildfire modeling helps managers decide where to build and maintain fuel breaks
summary: Fuel breaks are linear strips of land along which vegetation is cleared or thinned—constructed along ridgelines, roads and other strategic places—to give firefighters a better chance to safely slow or steer a fire. Often described as "speed bumps" for wildfires, fuel breaks rarely stop fire spread on their own, but they do give crews critical anchor points for building firelines, setting backfires or safely applying water and retardant. They have been used since the 1960s across many landscapes.

headline: New tool tracks unintended CRISPR edits and their effects in individual cells
summary: A new era of genome research began in 2012 with the discovery that CRISPR/Cas9 could function as molecular scissors to cut specific DNA sequences. Over time, scientists harnessed CRISPR as a genome-editing tool, which held the promise of precise gene removal and addition for research purposes, targeted therapies for genetic diseases like cystic fibrosis or Huntington's, and a future where personalized treatments are the norm. But a major shortcoming has snagged that progress: CRISPR can make off-target edits to parts of the genome never meant to be touched.

headline: Milk and wine used in Menorcan funerary rituals over 2,000 years ago
summary: In the Late Iron Age, or post-Talayotic period, over 2,000 years ago, Menorca and the other Balearic Islands experienced increasing connectivity with the wider Mediterranean. However, they also maintained distinctive local funerary traditions, such as burying their loved ones in rock-cut tombs, or artificial caves. Some of these caves contained external courtyards located in front of the burial chambers where animal offerings might have been made. Archaeologists even suspect that perishable foods or liquids were offered in characteristic island containers, such as high-bottomed vessels. Until now, however, the contents of these ceramic containers had never been identified.

headline: The experiments improving our understanding of volcanic tsunamis
summary: Tsunamis triggered by volcanic eruptions are poorly understood because of the complex dynamics governing how falling rocks and ash interact with seawater to generate waves. As a result, it is difficult to anticipate whether a volcanic flow will trigger a tsunami and, if so, how big it will be. Researchers have used laboratory experiments to study this process, but little is known about how well these models mimic reality.

headline: Climate response: Why previous warming makes all the difference

headline: Giant, prehistoric rodent fossils discovered in southern Thailand
summary: An international team of paleontologists, including researchers from McGill University, has discovered "remarkably large" rodent fossils in the pit of a mine in southern Thailand. The finding, published in Scientific Reports, provides a new perspective on the early manifestation of rodent gigantism—the process by which animals evolve to become larger—demonstrating that the evolutionary history of large-bodied rodents is considerably older and more geographically widespread than previously recognized, the researchers said.

headline: New observations challenge evidence for an 'outsize' black hole in the early universe
summary: A recent reanalysis of the outsize black hole galaxy UHZ1 using existing X-ray data and new infrared observations challenges a previous groundbreaking claim. Three years ago, this galaxy made news for hosting an unusually massive and heavily dust-obscured black hole formed through direct collapse. Led by Fan Zou of the University of Michigan, the new study reports no signs of hidden black hole activity. The paper, published in The Astrophysical Journal on Oct. 14, suggests UHZ1 could be a low-mass, metal-poor, star-forming galaxy.
